item.title: On equivalence between solution structures of the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.14469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an exact correspondence between the quasi-Wronskian and quasi-Grammian constructions for the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills (ASDYM) equations with complex \(2\times2\) matrix-valued fields. Starting from vacuum wave functions associated with \(2M\) pairwise distinct nonzero constant spectral parameters, we restrict attention to a nonempty local domain on which the corresponding interpolation matrix is invertible. We show that both constructions are governed by the same uniquely solvable matrix-polynomial interpolation problem. In particular, the quasi-Wronskian Darboux polynomial \(T(\lambda)\) and the quasi-Grammian rational dressing matrix \(W(\lambda)\) satisfy \[ T(\lambda)=q_\xi(\lambda)W(\lambda), \] where \(q_\xi(\lambda)\) is the monic scalar polynomial whose zeros are the prescribed poles of \(W(\lambda)\). This identity yields explicit relations between the corresponding Yang and potential matrices and shows that the two constructions generate identical ASDYM gauge potentials in the same gauge.
item.dc:creator: Shangshuai Li

item.title: Higher-order semi-rational solutions of the (2+1)-dimensional nonlocal multi-component Yajima--Oikawa system
item.description: arXiv:2610.14949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Higher-order semi-rational solutions are constructed for the (2+1)-dimensional nonlocal multi-component Yajima-Oikawa system. This system is obtained from its local \(2M\)-component counterpart through a spatial-reflection reduction. Using Hirota's bilinear method and the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili hierarchy reduction, we derive a unified \(6\times6\) block Gram determinant. Its entries involve Schur polynomials and exponential functions. The complex-conjugation and spatial-reflection reductions are imposed through algebraic constraints on the spectral parameters and determinant blocks, with the former ensuring a real-valued denominator tau function. Separate spectral parameter sets are assigned to the rational, breather, and dark-soliton blocks. These solutions describe paired lumps or line rogue waves on breather, dark-soliton, or combined backgrounds. Pure rational, breather, and dark-soliton solutions follow by setting the appropriate block sizes to zero. Asymptotic analysis establishes the elastic interactions of the fundamental breather and dark-soliton pairs and determines their position and phase shifts.
item.dc:creator: Wenqiang Lu, Kelei Tian, Ying Xu, Ge Yi, Xiaoming Zhu

item.title: Long-time asymptotics for the focusing coupled Kundu-Eckhaus equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The focusing coupled Kundu-Eckhaus (CKE) equation extends the coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CNLS) equation by adding quintic and derivative nonlinearities. We study the Cauchy problem for the focusing CKE equation with Schwartz initial data under the assumption of no discrete spectrum and no spectral singularities on the real axis. Based on the gauge equivalence between the focusing CKE and CNLS equations, we analyze the associated $3\times3$ matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem by the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method. By establishing joint error estimates for the CNLS solution and the gauge phase, we obtain a uniform long-time asymptotic formula for the dispersive radiation of the CKE equation with an $O(t^{-1}\log t)$ remainder in bounded velocity cones.
item.dc:creator: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang

item.title: Cetraro lectures on integrable systems and moduli spaces of curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.14608v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In these lecture notes we review some constructions and results on the relation between topology of the moduli space of stable curves and integrable systems of evolutionary PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Alexandr Buryak, Paolo Rossi

item.title: Bosonic Quantum Conditional Mutual Information and Bose-Einstein Condensation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16626v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article aims to introduce the bosonic asymmetric quantum conditional mutual information (QCMI), $I_{B}(A; B|C)$, as a rigorously defined information-theoretic quantity for continuous-variable (bosonic) systems. After defining $I_{B}(A; B|C)$ through quantum instruments on infinite-dimensional Fock spaces, we prove that Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) induces a logarithmic divergence $ I_{B}(A; B|C) \geq \alpha \log_2 (N_{0}^C+1)$, which further establishes $I_{B}(A; B|C)$ as a quantum-information order parameter for BEC with power-law scaling near the critical point. We provide the complete five-step proof of this result, connecting measurement back-action, off-diagonal long-range order, and Jensen's inequality. In the condensed phase, the effective causal propagation velocity is set by the Bogoliubov sound speed $c_s$ in the long-wavelength limit, and vanishes continuously at the superfluid--Mott-insulator transition. Applications to composite bosons, the BEC--BCS crossover, and a quantum-gas-microscope measurement protocol are presented. Finally, we demonstrate how the reduced bosonic QCMI serves as a finite-size scaling probe analogous to the Binder cumulant.
item.dc:creator: Anupam Ghosh

item.title: Experimental observation of ballistic correlations in integrable turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2601.21085v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Unequal-time correlation functions fundamentally characterize emergent statistical properties in complex systems, yet their direct measurement in experiments is challenging. We report the experimental observation of two-time, ballistic correlations in a photonic platform governed by the focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation. Using a recirculating optical fiber loop with heterodyne field detection, we acquire the full space-time dynamics of partially coherent optical waves and extract the intensity correlator in stationary states of integrable turbulence. The correlators collapse under ballistic rescaling and quantitatively agree with predictions from Generalized Hydrodynamics evaluated using the density of states obtained via inverse scattering analysis of the recorded fields. Our results provide a direct, parameter-free test of GHD in an integrable waves system.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Charnay et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 097202 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Elias Charnay, Adrien Escoubet, Francois Copie, Stephane Randoux, Thibault Bonnemain, Alvise Bastianello, Pierre Suret

item.title: The Korteweg-de Vries limit for the global dynamics of the Toda lattice
item.description: arXiv:2605.07532v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It has been observed that the dynamics of the Toda lattice can be well described by solutions of the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation in the continuum limit. We show that, under the KdV scaling and a suitable translation, the solution of the Toda lattice with H^1 initial data converges to that of the KdV equation globally in time. Our proof relies on tools from harmonic analysis and also on the construction and the conservation of mass and energy of the Toda lattice, the latter of which are derived from the completely integrable structure of the Toda lattice. As a consequence, we obtain long-wave KdV limits for the Toda lattice.
item.dc:creator: Herbert Koch, Ruoyuan Liu

item.title: Existence Conditions for Darboux Curves and Analytic First Integrals of a Li\'enard-Type Quadratic Vector Field
item.description:
arXiv:2609.13325v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the rational quadratic differential equation \[  rac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} =  rac{ay^2+by+cx}{y^2}, \qquad a,b,c\in\C, \] under the non-degeneracy assumptions \[ c
eq 0,\qquad 2ay+b
ot\equiv 0. \] Equivalently, after clearing the denominator, we consider the polynomial vector field \[ \dot{x}=y^2,\qquad \dot{y}=ay^2+by+cx. \] We give a complete, directly checkable classification of its Darboux curves. If $a=0$, no non-constant Darboux polynomial exists. If $a
eq 0$, a non-constant Darboux polynomial exists if and only if \[ c=-ab\qquad	ext{or}\qquad c=-2ab. \] In these two cases the unique irreducible Darboux polynomials, up to non-zero constant multiples, are respectively \[ y-ax,\qquad y^2-2bx. \] Consequently every non-constant Darboux polynomial is a non-zero constant multiple of a positive integral power of the corresponding irreducible factor. We then place this classification in the framework of Riccati (R-)integrability and rational potentials. Excluding the exceptional branch $c=-2ab$, the analytic integrability theorem identifies $c=-ab$ as the branch admitting a global Riccati-type analytic first integral. For $c=-2ab$, we compute the first four transverse variational groups along the transformed Darboux divisor over the rational function field. Their dimensions are $1,2,3,4$; the fourth is the full group of invertible fourth-order transverse jets. We prove that this exceptional branch admits no Riccati first integral and hence is not R-integrable. Finally, we relate the branch $c=-ab$ to the Quartic Inverse Riccati (QIR) class and discuss an invariant-based classification problem for quartic Abel equations.
item.dc:creator: Shaoxuan Huang

item.title: Maxwell's relations as Hamilton's equations: a symplectic and variational framework
item.description: arXiv:2609.18215v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a geometric framework in which classical thermodynamics is reformulated as a Hamiltonian dynamical system. An explicit canonical mapping $(q,p,t,H)\leftrightarrow(V,-P,S,-T)$ identifies Maxwell's relations as the characteristic equations of the thermodynamic Poincar\'e--Cartan one-form, in direct parallel with Hamilton's equations of motion. Treating thermodynamic potentials as action functionals, a variational principle recovers both the Maxwell relations and the thermodynamic constraints (adiabaticity, isothermality) as conserved first integrals. For adiabatic processes in an ideal gas, this yields explicit second-order ordinary differential equations for $V(T)$ and $P(T)$, each governed by a temperature-dependent Lagrangian. Assembling the component Lagrangians into a multi-parameter Lagrangian 1-form $\mathcal{L}$, we prove that the closure condition $d\mathcal{L}=0$ holds on the solution manifold, establishing that path-independence of thermodynamic state functions is a geometric consequence of multi-time integrability rather than an independent postulate.
item.dc:creator: Sikarin Yoo-Kong

item.title: Rational Q-systems at Root of Unity I. Closed Chains
item.description: arXiv:2310.14966v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The solution of Bethe ansatz equations for XXZ spin chain with the parameter $q$ being a root of unity is infamously subtle. In this work, we develop the rational $Q$-system for this case, which offers a systematic way to find all physical solutions of the Bethe ansatz equations at root of unity. The construction contains two parts. In the first part, we impose additional constraints to the rational $Q$-system. These constraints eliminate the so-called Fabricius-McCoy (FM) string solutions, yielding all primitive solutions. In the second part, we give a simple procedure to construct the descendant tower of any given primitive state. The primitive solutions together with their descendant towers constitute the complete Hilbert space. We test our proposal by extensive numerical checks and apply it to compute the torus partition function of the 6-vertex model at root of unity.
item.dc:creator: Jue Hou, Yunfeng Jiang, Yuan Miao

item.title: Twisted local G-wild mapping class groups
item.description: arXiv:2504.01701v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider isomonodromic-deformation parameters of irregular-singular connections on principal G-bundles over complex projective curves: for any connected reductive G, pole order, ramified formal normal form, and twist in the interior of the curve; covering the general setup of meromorphic reductive 2d gauge theory. We focus on the formal moduli, studying the deformation spaces of irregular types/classes at each pole: their fundamental groups are the eponymous local G-wild mapping class groups (G-WMCGs), akin to the complex braid groups of hyperplane arrangements \`a la Brou\'e--Malle--Rouquier. We prove that they sit in exact sequences involving `wild' versions of Weyl groups, and we parameterize their isomorphism classes via `Galois-closed' nested sequences of Levi subcosets \`a la Brou\'e--Malle--Michel. This relies on Lehrer--Springer theory, and in the quasigeneric case yields new modular interpretations of complex reflection groups and of Bessis' braid-group lift. The subregular regime still yields complex reflections in `relative' Springer theory, provided an obstruction vanishes in Howlett theory; but in general one exits the reflection realm. We also introduce new fission trees to treat structure groups of any classical type, after relating with Bell/Stirling numbers, classifying the resulting hyperplane arrangements and describing the local G-WMCGs explicitly. In particular we single out an infinite family of nonreflection examples in type D: they remain K(pi,1) by work of Amend--Deligne--R\"ohrle, fitting the modular viewpoint of `wild' Teichm\"uller spaces in Boalch's theory of wild curves. Finally, we extend all of this to the interior twists. Algebraically, this yields a nonsplit setup where the Weyl group is twisted by an infinitesimal outer automorphism of G, so that fission takes place in a proper reflection coset.
item.dc:creator: Jean Dou\c{c}ot, Gabriele Rembado, Daisuke Yamakawa

item.title: Accessing Levinson-Smith and Li\'{e}nard equations in a nonlinear framework of quantum mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2602.04747v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we present the reduction of a recently introduced generalized quantum scheme of Chodos and Cooper to Levinson-Smith and Li\'{e}nard classes of nonlinear system that enable us to furnish a wider class of acceptable solutions. In particular, for the Levinson-Smith equations, we find their relevance to position-dependent mass quantum systems, with an interesting off-shoot that solitonic-like solutions emerge from the condition of the level surface in the system. On the other hand, for the Li\'{e}nard type, which has coefficients of odd and odd symmetry in the present set up, we demonstrate that closed form solutions exist on carrying out conversion to the typical Abel form.
item.dc:creator: Bijan Bagchi, Anindya Ghose-Choudhury

item.title: Integrable multi-species SSEP with reactive particle species
item.description: arXiv:2607.18959v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate integrable exclusion Markov processes constructed from set-theoretical solutions of the Yang-Baxter Equation (YBE) that generalise the multi-species Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (SSEP). We first introduce the process called the $ (p,1) $-SSEP that is analogous to the multi-species SSEP but with an extra particle species qualified as reactive. Reactive species are able to evaporate and condense by pairs or to transform by pairs depending on the interpretation. We provide a full combinatorial study of the sectors in the periodic case. We prove the integrability of the process in the periodic case and in the open case for two types of boundaries that we introduce using Baxterisations of solutions of the reflection equation. Next we move on to the process called $ (p,q) $-SSEP, i.e. the multi-species SSEP with an arbitrary number of reactive particle species. We prove its integrability in the periodic case and, for the open case, we introduce integrable boundaries generalising the ones considered for the $ (p,1) $-SSEP. Finally, we define physical quantities relevant to the models and we compute them in the non-equilibrium stationary state of the open $ (p,q) $-SSEP for one type of integrable boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dabrowski, Lo\"ic Poulain d'Andecy, Eric Ragoucy

item.title: Integrable Chiral Quantum Field Theories with Spacetime-Dependent Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2609.13377v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a class of integrable chiral fermionic quantum field theories with interactions that depend on both space and time. The construction starts from a unitary, regular, difference-form two-body scattering matrix satisfying braiding unitarity and the Yang--Baxter equation. Each freely moving right- or left-moving particle carries a characteristic coordinate that remains constant along its trajectory, and the scattering matrix depends on differences of these coordinates. The many-body amplitudes form a discrete connection over the coordinate-ordering sectors. The Yang--Baxter equation gives local path independence, while periodic winding on a spatial circle produces quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (qKZ) difference equations expressing global flatness. Once a reference amplitude satisfying the exchange and qKZ constraints is specified, these transport equations determine the exact wavefunction in every fixed-particle-number sector. Independent reparametrizations of the right- and left-moving characteristics give couplings that depend on both space and time. For the chiral $SU(2)$ Gross--Neveu realization, we solve the qKZ equations for this full characteristic family using off-shell Bethe vectors. The resulting amplitudes are written in the characteristic labels, and their pullbacks give exact many-body wavefunctions for the corresponding space-time-dependent couplings. The two-body amplitude is a ratio of Gamma functions that resums the phase shifts from successive scattering processes. Equal-slope affine maps give a spatially homogeneous specialization in which the coupling depends only on time, and the Bethe ansatz with constant coupling is recovered when the qKZ step vanishes.
item.dc:creator: Pradip Kattel
